name: Cardboard Pizza Boxes
summary: Cardboard is recyclable, but food grease and cheese oils permanently ruin paper recycling pulp batches.
instructions: Tear the box in half along the hinge: clean top lid goes into Blue Cart; greasy bottom goes into Black Cart trash or compost.
diyTip: The greasy cardboard bottom can be torn into strips and layered at the bottom of raised garden beds or planters as sheet mulch to suppress weeds.

name: Lithium-Ion & Rechargeable Batteries
summary: Never put lithium batteries in your Blue Cart or alley dumpster. They easily crush during transport, sparking explosive truck fires.
instructions: Cover exposed metal terminals with standard clear tape or electrical tape before drop-off to eliminate spark hazards.

location.name: The Home Depot (Call2Recycle Drop Box)
location.address: Enter your ZIP code to find the nearest hardware drop box.
location.notes: Collection box usually located right inside the entrance vestibule near customer service.

name: Plastic Grocery Bags & Film
summary: The #1 cause of recycling contamination in Chicago. Loose plastic film wraps around sorting gears, shutting down sorting lines.
instructions: Never bag recyclables in plastic. Clean, dry grocery bags and shrink wrap must be returned to collection bins at local grocery stores.
diyTip: Save clean bags to line small bathroom wastebaskets or keep inside winter boots and purses to preserve their shape in storage.

location.name: Grocery & Retail Film Return
location.address: Enter your ZIP code to find the nearest store drop-off.
location.notes: Place clean, dry plastic grocery bags directly into collection bins located in front entrance vestibules.

name: Glass Bottles & Jars
summary: Accepted in Chicago curbside Blue Carts. Glass is 100% infinitely recyclable without loss of quality.
instructions: Empty and rinse clean. Metal lids can be detached and recycled loose in the Blue Cart. Do not break.
diyTip: Rinse wide-mouth pickle and sauce jars for bulk pantry storage or water propagation stations for houseplants like pothos.
reuseIntro: Before tossing clean jars into the Blue Cart, reuse them for pantry staples, olive oils, and soaps at Chicago zero-waste refill stores:

reusePartners.name: The Refilleri
reusePartners.tagline: Low-waste grocer & refill bar for bulk pantry staples, olive oils, and household soaps.

reusePartners.name: The Eco Flamingo
reusePartners.tagline: Zero-waste general store. Bring clean, dry jars to weigh and fill from bulk gravity hoppers.

reusePartners.name: The Unwaste Shop
reusePartners.tagline: Modern sustainable shop offering liquid household cleaning refills, personal care, and bulk teas.

reusePartners.name: Dill Pickle Food Co-op
reusePartners.tagline: Community grocery featuring bulk gravity bins for grains, beans, nuts, and spices.

name: Oil-Based Paint, Wood Stains & Thinners
summary: Highly flammable and hazardous. Strictly prohibited from curbside recycling carts, trash dumpsters, and city sewer drains.
instructions: Must be kept in original, sealed containers with readable labels. Bring directly to the Goose Island HCCRF facility.

location.name: Chicago HCCRF (Goose Island)
location.address: 1150 N North Branch St, Chicago, IL 60642
location.notes: Open Tuesdays 7am–12pm, Thursdays 2pm–7pm, and 1st Saturday of each month 8am–3pm. Only city facility for oil paint.

name: Mattresses & Box Springs
summary: Prohibited from Blue Carts. Leaving mattresses loose in alleys triggers city sanitation citations and hauler fines.
instructions: Must be sealed in a plastic mattress bag if set out for municipal bulk collection, or booked through an on-demand hauling service.

location.name: LoadUp On-Demand Pickup
location.address: Direct in-home or alley pickup across Chicago
location.notes: Upfront guaranteed pricing. Avoids city alley tickets.

name: Food Scraps & Organics
summary: Food waste is completely prohibited from Blue Carts. In landfills, organic waste decomposes anaerobically into methane.
instructions: Drop off at city community food scrap bins or subscribe to a residential bucket pickup service.

compostPartners.name: WasteNot Compost
compostPartners.tagline: Zero-emissions electric fleet residential bucket swaps right at your doorstep.

compostPartners.name: The Urban Canopy
compostPartners.tagline: South Side urban farm collecting scraps to rebuild local community soil.

compostPartners.name: Block Bins
compostPartners.tagline: Affordable shared green bins secured with combination locks placed in residential alleys.

diyTip: Collect vegetable trimmings in a freezer bag; boil for 45 mins when full to make rich homemade vegetable stock.

name: Televisions & Large Electronics
summary: Under the Illinois Electronic Products Recycling Act, it is illegal to landfill televisions and computer monitors.
instructions: Drop off during open public hours at Goose Island or schedule a bulk electronics haul.

location.name: Chicago HCCRF (Goose Island)
location.address: 1150 N North Branch St, Chicago, IL 60642
location.notes: Tuesdays 7am–12pm, Thursdays 2pm–7pm, 1st Saturday of each month 8am–3pm.

name: Latex & Water-Based Wall Paint
summary: Latex paint is water-based and non-hazardous. Because of this, it is REJECTED at Goose Island.
instructions: Must be solidified before disposal. Mix with kitty litter or paint hardener until rock hard, then place lid-off in the Black Cart.
diyTip: Post usable leftover paint on neighborhood Buy Nothing groups or offer it to local Chicago community theaters and school drama departments.

name: Used Motor Oil & Fluids
summary: Illegal to dump down alley drains or sewers. Automotive parts retailers accept used motor oil for free drop-off.
instructions: Store in a clean container with a tight cap. Bring up to 5 gallons to your nearest auto parts store.

location.name: AutoZone Parts Drop-Off
location.address: Enter your ZIP code to find the nearest participating store.
location.notes: Free used motor oil collection up to 5 gallons per customer.
